sources.name: OS Downloads API Overview
sources.role: Automated discovery, metadata and download-link access contract for OS OpenData and data packages
verified_facts: OS Downloads API exposes available OS OpenData products, product metadata and download links.
It supports automated retrieval and integration workflows across multiple coverage areas and formats.
The overview distinguishes OpenData discovery/download operations from premium data-package operations.
semantic_limits: API availability or product discovery does not prove that a selected file was fully downloaded.
An advertised format or area is not evidence that the exact Terrain 50 tile used by the runner is correct.
Download metadata must remain bound to the resulting file name, area, release and digest.

sources.name: OS Downloads API Technical Specification
sources.role: Authentication boundary, endpoint families and current-content discovery contract
verified_facts: OS OpenData endpoints do not require an API key, while premium data-package endpoints require authentication.
The specification separates product listing, product details, download listing and thumbnail operations.
Clients are directed to query current API content because available products can change.
semantic_limits: Unauthenticated access does not establish publisher-file integrity after transfer.
A successful endpoint response does not prove complete ZIP, nested file or raster validation.
Current product discovery must not be confused with exact release-byte pinning.

sources.name: OS Downloads API OpenData Products
sources.role: OpenData product-list and expanded product-metadata response contract
verified_facts: The endpoint returns the OpenData products currently available to download.
The optional expanded parameter requests full product details in the listing response.
A successful response is represented as a collection of product information objects.
semantic_limits: A product-list entry is discovery metadata, not a downloaded terrain object.
Product presence does not establish exact geographic coverage for a parcel.
List-response freshness does not replace exact download receipt and digest.

sources.name: OS Downloads API OpenData Product Details
sources.role: Single-product identifier and metadata readback contract
verified_facts: The endpoint returns details for a specific OpenData product identifier.
An unknown product request returns a not-found response rather than a valid product object.
The response describes information about a product made available through the API.
semantic_limits: Product metadata does not prove that a particular download belongs to the requested release.
A valid product identifier is not a National Grid tile binding.
Metadata readback must remain separate from raster sampling evidence.

sources.name: OS Downloads API Download an OpenData Product
sources.role: Download-list filtering by file, format, subformat and National Grid area contract
verified_facts: The endpoint returns downloads for a specific OpenData product.
Downloads can be filtered by file name, format, subformat and geographic area.
Area values include National Grid squares such as TQ, and an optional redirect can target a single selected download.
semantic_limits: A 307 redirect is a transport step and not proof of final-object completeness.
Area TQ identifies a broad download region and not an exact parcel polygon.
Filters must be read back and the returned bytes hashed before acceptance.

sources.name: OS Terrain 50 Documentation
sources.role: Product publication cycle, coverage, formats and access contract
verified_facts: OS Terrain 50 is an OpenData digital terrain model product covering Great Britain.
The product is updated annually in July.
Grid data uses 50 metre post spacing and the product is supplied through OS Data Hub.
semantic_limits: Annual publication does not prove that a local cached file is the current July release.
Product coverage does not establish that all cells intersecting a parcel were sampled.
OpenData access does not replace tile-level receipt and digest verification.

sources.name: OS Terrain 50 Overview
sources.role: Lower-resolution DTM, 50 metre spacing, tile and update-frequency contract
verified_facts: OS Terrain 50 is designed for landscape visualisation and analysis over large areas.
Grid and contour products are supplied as 10 kilometre by 10 kilometre National Grid tiles.
The product is updated annually in July and provides full Great Britain coverage.
semantic_limits: Terrain 50 is a coarse screening source and must not replace EA DTM 1 metre parcel measurements.
Tile coverage does not imply exact parcel containment.
Full-country coverage does not prove that a particular tile payload is present or valid.

sources.name: OS Terrain 50 Technical Specification
sources.role: Grid/contour supply format, 10 kilometre tile and archive-contents contract
verified_facts: Terrain 50 grid and contour forms are produced from the same source data.
The 50 metre grid is supplied in ASCII grid and GML 3.2.1.
Geographic tiles are delivered as compressed folders containing data and additional files.
semantic_limits: Shared source lineage does not make contour and grid values interchangeable.
A compressed folder must be checked for expected nested files and exact tile identity.
GML presence does not prove that the external ASCII grid was parsed correctly.

sources.name: INSPIRE Index Polygons Dataset
sources.role: Monthly publication, GML access and indicative freehold extent contract
verified_facts: The INSPIRE Index Polygons dataset is published as GML files.
New files are published on the first Sunday of each month and show the previous month's data.
The dataset is intended for use in geographic information systems.
semantic_limits: Monthly publication does not make polygons exact legal boundaries.
A current landing page does not prove that all required local-authority files were downloaded.
GML availability does not establish exact target-row binding.

sources.name: INSPIRE Index Polygons Download
sources.role: Published-date, local-authority file and Open Government Licence acquisition contract
verified_facts: The current download page identifies a publication dated 5 July 2026.
Polygons are downloadable by local authority.
The data describes the indicative extent and position of registered freehold properties in England and Wales.
semantic_limits: A local-authority archive must be pinned to publication date, file name and digest.
Indicative extent must not be represented as a determined legal boundary.
Download-page freshness does not prove successful extraction or point-in-polygon matching.

sources.name: INSPIRE GML Technical Guidance
sources.role: Native British National Grid geometry, conversion and reprojection-error contract
verified_facts: HM Land Registry captures the polygon data against British National Grid.
GIS tools can convert GML into other formats and projections.
The guidance warns that British National Grid to WGS84 conversion can shift some features by up to 15 metres.
semantic_limits: Native EPSG:27700 geometry must be used for exact parcel containment.
Converted display geometry must not silently replace the source polygon.
Successful format conversion does not prove source identity or geometry fidelity.

sources.name: LIDAR Composite Digital Terrain Model 1m
sources.role: Primary DTM resolution, survey lineage, tiling, datum and vertical-accuracy contract
verified_facts: The DTM is a one metre raster elevation model covering approximately 99 percent of England.
It combines time-stamped archive and National LIDAR Programme surveys and uses newer, better-resolution data where repeat surveys exist.
Data is supplied as 5 kilometre GeoTIFF tiles in metres, aligned to the OS National Grid, referenced to Ordnance Datum Newlyn using OSTN15.
semantic_limits: Composite pixels can derive from surveys of different dates and require location-specific metadata.
The plus or minus 15 centimetre RMSE statement is not a guarantee for each pixel.
The landing page does not prove the exact GeoTIFF object and sampling receipt.

sources.name: Persistent LIDAR Composite WCS Endpoint Announcement
sources.role: Persistent WCS endpoint, WMS portrayal separation and service-migration contract
verified_facts: Environment Agency replaced Esri Image Services with open-standard WCS and WMS services.
WCS provides elevation data while WMS provides a summarised portrayal.
The LIDAR Composite DTM 1 metre service uses a persistent endpoint without a release-year suffix.
semantic_limits: A persistent endpoint can change underlying content and must be queried with exact coverage identity.
WMS imagery must not be sampled as numeric elevation.
WCS success does not prove complete payload, CRS, range field or source digest.

sources.name: National LIDAR Programme
sources.role: National one-metre survey programme, phase, CRS and publication contract
verified_facts: The programme provides one metre elevation data for all of England.
Phase 1 survey blocks were captured between January 2017 and February 2023.
Repeat surveys receive incrementing phase numbers and data is published through the Defra portal on an ongoing quarterly basis.
semantic_limits: National coverage does not mean uniform survey date or phase.
Programme membership does not identify the exact source survey for a parcel.
Quarterly publication does not prove a local raster is current.

sources.name: LiDAR Vertical Accuracy Guidance
sources.role: Absolute and relative LiDAR height-error budget contract
verified_facts: Environment Agency specifications require absolute height error below plus or minus 15 centimetres RMSE.
Absolute error is assessed against Ground Truth Survey data.
Expected relative random height error is no more than plus or minus 5 centimetres.
semantic_limits: Specification thresholds are uncertainty inputs rather than parcel-specific certification.
Relative error must not be conflated with absolute datum accuracy.
Accuracy guidance does not validate an unexecuted sampling run.

sources.name: LiDAR Projection Information
sources.role: OSGB36, ODN, OSTN15 and survey-era geoid contract
verified_facts: Environment Agency data is supplied in OSGB36 British National Grid with elevations above Ordnance Datum Newlyn.
The LiDAR Composite uses OSTN15.
Surveys after 26 August 2016 use OSGM15, while older time-stamped data requires survey-specific metadata.
semantic_limits: Survey-era geoid metadata must not be inferred from composite publication date.
Horizontal transformation correctness does not establish vertical surface accuracy.
Datum declarations do not replace raster-byte and pixel-validity checks.

sources.name: DSP Dataset Metadata Guidance
sources.role: Dataset summary, limitation, licence and metadata-field interpretation contract
verified_facts: Every dataset published on the Data Services Platform is accompanied by a metadata record.
Metadata describes the dataset, use limitations, categories, keywords and licence information.
Metadata is intended to help users understand how data should be used and its limitations.
semantic_limits: Metadata describes a dataset and is not the numeric raster payload.
Metadata completeness does not prove object-byte completeness.
A licence or summary field must not be promoted to measurement evidence.

sources.name: LiDAR GeoPackage Metadata Index Update
sources.role: GeoPackage spatial metadata index, temporal extent and archive-content contract
verified_facts: LiDAR Composite and SurfZone download ZIP files now contain spatial metadata indexes in GeoPackage format.
The index describes the spatial location and temporal extent of raster elevation data.
Technical guides describe the index format and attribute schema.
semantic_limits: A GeoPackage index is metadata and not the elevation raster.
Spatial index coverage does not prove that all raster files are present and valid.
Container integrity must remain separate from height-measurement accuracy.

sources.name: OGC Web Coverage Service Standard
sources.role: Coverage core, implementation schema and encoding-extension contract
verified_facts: OGC WCS standards provide access to multidimensional coverage data.
The standards family separates core service requirements from coverage implementation schemas.
Encoding profiles include formats such as GeoTIFF, JPEG2000 and CF-netCDF.
semantic_limits: Service and encoding conformance do not establish terrain authority or parcel accuracy.
Coverage range type and envelope do not prove exact range values or parcel geometry.
Complete payload, CRS, datum, units and digest remain required.

sources.publisher: National Institute of Standards and Technology
sources.name: FIPS 180-4 Secure Hash Standard
sources.role: SHA message-digest and post-digest change-detection contract
verified_facts: FIPS 180-4 specifies secure hash algorithms used to generate message digests.
Message digests can be used to detect whether messages changed after digest generation.
The final publication is dated August 2015 and supersedes the March 2012 edition.
semantic_limits: A matching digest establishes byte identity only for the exact hashed object and algorithm.
Hash equality does not prove publisher authority, semantic correctness or measurement accuracy.
Digest evidence must remain bound to acquisition time, source identity and execution receipts.
